We came to drop off our cat, and were very well received. We were told that we would be notified when the cat was ready to be picked up. We were there on time but there was no one at the reception. We couldn't get a hold of anyone when we knocked on all the doors repeatedly. It took 50 minutes before someone came out and we got him back. We were told that it took longer because another animal needed urgent help, which is very understandable. But by then it had been 5 hours since he had been to the bathroom (and he both peed and pooped just before we left home). When we got home 15 minutes later we discovered that he had peed and pooped in his cage, and he was very dirty. The first thing he did when we got home was run to the bathroom. We had to throw away the blanket and toys he brought with him, but we couldn't shower him because of the surgery. It was a lot of trouble 😓

This is the first time we've had an animal, and we're wondering if the animals don't get a chance to go to the bathroom at the vet?

Worst Veterinary Clinic in Oslo – Avoid at All Costs

We’ve had problems with this clinic both times we visited — for two different situations — and each time the experience was stressful, overpriced, and unprofessional.

First Visit – Travel Check for My Dog
Before a trip, I brought my dog in for a standard check. He has two microchips because as a puppy, the first one didn’t work. Only the second chip was recorded in his passport.

This vet scanned him, saw that both chips were now working, and immediately told me I couldn’t travel because only one chip number was in the passport. She insisted I had to get a completely new passport listing both chip numbers — otherwise, I would face “administrative problems at the airport.”

Then she tried to sell me a “travel certificate” for about €100, claiming airlines in Europe would demand it, even though the airline’s own website didn’t list it as a requirement. By the end of this so-called “check-up,” the bill was already at €300.

Later, I spoke to my regular vet (who was on sick leave at the time) and learned that:

You cannot just replace a passport if it has existing valid vaccinations, because the original proof must remain in the original passport.

Having two chips is not a problem; the correct solution is to add the second chip number to the current passport — no need for an expensive new one.
In other words, everything this clinic told me was misleading and unnecessary.

Second Visit – Nail Clipping Disaster
On another occasion, I brought my dog in for nail clipping. He’s anxious, so we have a specific method that works. The staff member, Heda, seemed unsure of what she was doing. She managed to clip just one nail out of twenty, then suggested I return another day for sedation.

When I asked if we could just do sedation now, she refused and said I’d be charged for both today’s failed attempt and the sedation visit later. When I questioned why I should pay full price for a job that wasn’t done, she said I had to pay for “her time.”

To me, that’s outrageous. Professionals get paid for doing their job, not for failing and making the customer come back twice. Instead of taking responsibility, she acted offended that I even questioned the charge.

Final Verdict
This clinic is overpriced, unhelpful, and quick to upsell unnecessary procedures. Their staff seems more focused on charging for every minute than actually helping animals.
Do yourself and your pet a favor — go somewhere else.

Another encounter with an industry that for many seems to be stripped of knowledge, morals and empathy. Here, as with all the larger chains, it didn't take long before I was met by yet another newly qualified veterinary "temporary". Who seemed to lack the craftsmanship, knowledge, and even the interest in taking samples of my dog's earwax. I had to do it myself, but was even interrupted before I had time to collect any. - The examination was thus inconclusive, but was still billed for, and the standard procedure for general cleaning and reduction of inflammation that had already been initiated was maintained. - But I could come back to have the cortisone in the cleaning fluid topped up. Which I did the next day, and this is where the story really begins: No one in the store premises a quarter of an hour before closing time, so I knocked on the office doors to make contact. After a few minutes, a young lady comes out and invites me in to look at the records to find the necessary mixing ratio since she herself could not answer what was intended. Since this information was not listed in the record, I asked her to contact our last veterinarian to have this clarified, but she could not do so at first because “she was in a meeting”, which soon changed to because “it was after her working hours”… I pointed out angrily that this would delay the treatment of a troublesome ear infection and that I would therefore contact management. The next day, before I could get that far, I was called by a Swedish lady who was primarily looking for an excuse as to why I had been all the way to her office so late at night (within opening hours)…. The "misunderstanding" was cleared up without any apology from her, but one from me about her assistant's (who shouldn't have been able to mix medications anyway) reaction... - Completely searched..., but what can't you do to get clarification and progress. I then waited for several hours without hearing anything before I contacted them again out of concern that the treatment would have to be postponed for another day. Only to be dismissed with a sour response that the treatment had been changed and that I would receive an email and a requisition for a new preparation. I naturally wanted to know what this new treatment entailed, but was strictly told to wait for a letter. After a few minutes, the then missing epicrisis came ticking in, but no separate requisition (in their defense, I later saw that it is mentioned at the bottom of the epicrisis that such a one has been called in). So I called again, only to be met again with the same attitude and an ignorant demand to continue waiting for the requisition just before closing time. I imagine a third day without cortisone and now (finally) slam my hand on the table to insist on an explanation, but am interrupted with anger and the message that I am not wanted back ….
Quite hair-raising? Nothing compared to what I and so many others have experienced with their loved ones at these vets. Endless stories… But still. Choose for yourself. I myself will now find myself a small veterinary office where I always know who will take care of my dog, and where the animal's interests come first. Not the money.
